lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: bisectors, perpendiculars, and parallels through a point
lessonRef.title: Targeted correction: bisectors, perpendiculars, and parallels through a point

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Each example contains the correction, not just the answer.

steps: Fix a centre and a distance.
Take every point in the plane at that distance.
workedSolution.answer: the set of points at a fixed distance from a centre

items.prompt: Equal arcs from A and B meet above and below AB. What is the joining line?

steps: Both meeting points are equidistant from A and B.
That locus is the perpendicular bisector.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Before solving, say which error the problem is testing for.

items.prompt: A regular triangle is inscribed in a circle of radius 4. What central angle does each side subtend?
Which statement correctly justifies the angle bisector construction?
choices: The ray drawn appears to split the angle evenly.
The construction relies on the angle being acute.
The construction builds two congruent triangles by SSS, so the angles at the vertex are congruent.
Equal arcs always produce equal angles regardless of the triangle.

items.prompt: Which statement is a precise definition of a circle?
choices: a shape whose area is πr²
a polygon with infinitely many sides
the set of all points in a plane at a fixed distance from a given centre point
a closed curve with no corners

items.prompt: A construction proceeds as follows. From vertex V draw an arc crossing both rays at P and Q. From P and Q draw equal arcs meeting at R. Draw ray VR. What has been constructed?
choices: a line perpendicular to one ray
the bisector of the angle at V
the perpendicular bisector of PQ only
an equilateral triangle on PQ

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A regular hexagon is inscribed in a circle of radius 12. What central angle does each side subtend?
Which statement correctly justifies the equilateral triangle construction on a given segment?
choices: The intersection point is the midpoint of the segment.
The construction works only when the segment is horizontal.
The circles intersect, which guarantees 60° angles by definition.
Both circles have radius equal to the segment, so all three sides are that same length.

items.prompt: Which statement is a precise definition of a perpendicular lines?
choices: two lines with opposite slopes
two lines that never meet
two lines that form an isosceles triangle
two lines that intersect to form right angles

items.prompt: A construction proceeds as follows. Through point P not on line ℓ, copy the angle that a transversal makes with ℓ, placing the copy at P on the same transversal. What has been constructed?
choices: the reflection of ℓ across P
the perpendicular bisector of the transversal
a line through P parallel to ℓ
a line through P perpendicular to ℓ
